verdicts.trueWording: The homes of notable NPCs get pages of room descriptions
verdicts.note: Raw page (live, browser UA). Verbatim in section 'Matching description to a location's purpose', of Curse of Strahd. Post footer dates it November 21, 2016, not the claim's 2018-2020.

verdicts.trueWording: page-long description of his workroom in the 5-page description
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim; the measurement (page-long workroom inside a 5-page mansion) is exact. The page names only 'the players' ally Victor Wachter'; 'Vallaki' appears nowhere on it (0 hits). Post dated November 21, 2016.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: the page never places Victor Wachter, or his father's mansion, in Vallaki

verdicts.trueWording: Read the flavor text out loud
verdicts.note: Raw page. Verbatim under 'Chapter 3: The Village of Barovia', bullet 'When the Heroes Arrive : (page 41)'. Post dated Friday, March 25, 2016.

verdicts.trueWording: Spread over more than 150 pages, we get a full description
verdicts.note: Raw page. Verbatim in section 'Setting'; the sentence continues to each of Ten-Towns plus 13 wilderness adventure locations, matching both limbs.

verdicts.trueWording: nearly every location has a meaningful quest or event attached
verdicts.note: Raw page, section 'Setting'. HTML splits the word across a styled span ('n' + '<span>early'), so the text reads 'nearly'; the claim's 'nearly every' is correct.

verdicts.trueWording: very hard to use directly at the table
verdicts.note: Quote 'long, meandering, and poorly-structured paragraphs of text' is verbatim in section 'Accessibility'. The page grades the difficulty, not impossibility.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'cannot be used at the table' overstates the page's 'very hard to use directly at the table'

verdicts.trueWording: each town only gets 2 or 3 described locations
verdicts.note: Raw page. Verbatim in section 'Ten-Towns Businesses & NPCs', explicitly of Rime's ten towns. Post dated November 2020.

verdicts.trueWording: each town write-up comes with at least one new NPC per location
verdicts.note: Raw page, section 'NPCs', whose paragraph subject is Legacy of the Crystal Shard's campaign guide ('In this supplement we meet...'). The year 2013 is the claim's own editorial gloss; the page names the product but no year.

verdicts.trueWording: the Armory and Council Hall in Bryn Shander get 2-3 sentences each
verdicts.note: Raw page, section 'Ten-Towns Businesses & NPCs'. Context puts both among the extra locations Legacy adds ('presents all of these plus 17 more'), and calls those write-ups 'not extensive', supporting 'minor'.

verdicts.trueWording: The DMG divides settlements just by population
verdicts.note: Raw page, section 'Village'; the preceding sentence names 'The 5e DMG', and the quoted sentence continues 'and lumps together everything under 1,000 inhabitants as a village'.

verdicts.trueWording: as described in the Commerce section (p19)
verdicts.note: Raw page, section 'Village'. The article walks the DMG's settlement-generation section by heading (Purpose p15, Size with Village/Town/City sub-headings, Commerce p19), supporting both limbs.

verdicts.trueWording: Baron Vargas Vallakovich, the Burgomaster of Vallaki, a ruthless cruel man
verdicts.note: Live URL 403; recovered via Wayback raw capture 20260418221915id_. Verbatim under heading 'The powers at play'. Title, given name, surname, then office - all four limbs on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: the "guard" consists of Izek and 24 guards
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture. Quote verbatim under heading 'The Bomb in Vallaki'. 'captain' and 'commander' return 0 hits on the page; Izek is named only as distinct from the 24 guards, and elsewhere as Ireena's brother.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'captain' - the page gives Izek no rank, title or command role

verdicts.trueWording: Reading out a chunk of boxed text is basically equivalent to waving
verdicts.note: Raw page, thread 'Boxed texts'. The sentence continues to a flag reading that the location or NPC is a clue to the plot, supporting the claim. Post is by 'humble minion', dated Jul 12, 2020, not the claim's 2021.

Raw page, closing assessment, dated November 7th, 2018. Framed counterfactually ('could have easily been a 64 page module plus...'), but the next sentence treats it as the book's own usable 96 pages, so the gazetteer estimate does attach to Dragon Heist.
